payload.claim: [host-filed criterion probe] tests/test_prose_limit_hook.py::test_lint_runs_the_tree_hook_after_a_failure_and_still_fails stayed green with the spec's wrong version 'A second call of `prek run --all-files --stage manual` with no hook id, which reruns every hook, `prose-limit` included.' applied to Makefile as an edit. The claim was '`make lint` calls prek twice, in order, whichever way the first call ends. The first is `prek run --all-files --skip prose-limit`. The second is `prek run --all-files --stage manual prose-limit-tree`. The recipe exits non-zero when either call fails, and 0 when both pass. The witness runs the `lint` recipe from `Makefile` as make would, against a stub `prek` on `PATH` that logs its arguments. It drives three cases. Both calls pass, the first fails, and the second fails. Each case logs both calls, and only the first case exits 0.', and only that witness ran under the edit.
